root.name: Benko Gambit Accepted: Central Storming Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 b5 4. cxb5 a6 5. bxa6 g6 6. Nc3 Bxa6 7. f4

overview: White accepts the gambit pawn and plays 7.f4 to take the whole centre with e4 and a later e5 or f5 push, giving up the quiet development of the main lines. Black has the usual Benko compensation: open a- and b-files, the long diagonal with ...Bg7 and pressure on the queenside. Black normally plays ...d6 and ...Bg7 and watches for a central break, while White castles and tries to get e4-e5 in before Black's pieces are active.

white_ideas.idea: Build a pawn centre with e4 and f4, then push e5 or f5
Use the extra pawn but meet ...Bxf1 and ...Qa5 with Nf3 and Be2

black_ideas.idea: Long-term pressure on the a- and b-files with ...Rb8 and ...Qa5
Fianchetto the bishop and strike the centre with ...d6 and ...Nbd7

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on d5, e4, f4 against a Black fianchetto and half-open a- and b-files

character.notes: White's centre storm and Black's counter play on the queenside are both concrete; this is an unbalanced fight rather than a slow manoeuvring one.

gambit.notes: Black is a pawn down after 6...Bxa6 and gets compensation instead of regaining the pawn directly.

soundness.notes: The Benko is accepted as sound; the compensation is real even against the f4 set-up.

structure.notes: The d5 wedge, a-file and b-file are half-open, and the centre is fixed asymmetrically.

level.notes: Compensation is positional and hard to judge but the line itself has modest theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Fianchetto Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 b5 4. cxb5 a6 5. bxa6 Bxa6 6. Nc3 g6 7. g3

character.reason: White's f4 central expansion against Black's open queenside lines leads to concrete play.

gambit.reason: Black is a pawn down for open lines and has not regained it.

soundness.reason: The Benko is considered fully sound and the compensation holds against f4.

structure.reason: Half-open a- and b-files with the d5 wedge give a fixed asymmetric centre.

approach.reason: Played by strong players as a mainstream Black weapon.

level.reason: Compensation is positional but the f4 line has limited forced theory.

plans.reason: Black pressures along the queenside files; the c-file is a loose approximation of the half-open files.
